text: Prooflane checks router and firewall settings, flags security
risks, and shows the evidence behind every finding.
Here is how it works.
Different vendors use different configuration languages.
Reviewing them by hand makes security problems easy to
miss.
Upload saved device settings.
Add the device type, software version and file completeness.
Choose a security checklist, then start the audit.
In this sample, line five uses an old version
of secure remote access, SSH.
The rule requires version two.
Prooflane flags the mismatch and suggests a fix for
human review.
Missing or conflicting evidence stays unknown.
The coverage bar shows how much could actually be
checked.
Inspect findings beside the original settings, compare what was
found with what was expected, and download a shareable
report.
When a format is unfamiliar, Gemini consults approved
references and asks questions.
It proposes a rule for reading that format.
Tests and a human reviewer must approve it before
use.
Approved reading rules work without a code deployment.
Every audit keeps its original input and rule versions,
even when later rules change.
Explore the audit in three dimensions.
Select any stage to see the recorded evidence behind
it.
The interface sends audits to background workers.
A database keeps their history.
Encrypted storage protects files.
Access is controlled by role.
Optional AI helps investigate unfamiliar formats.
Twenty checks cover selected Cisco, Junos and FortiOS settings.
Synthetic tests covered sustained load and recovery.
Standards crosswalks support review;
they do not certify compliance.
Prooflane.
Trace the finding.
Trust the evidence.
